t: This is the church of St John-at-Hackney, a large Grade Two star listed building built in 1792. It replaced Hackney's medieval parish church, and if you look to the edge of the churchyard you can still see that older church's tower, St Augustine's. The architect was James Spiller, a close associate of Sir John Soane. Today it is both a working parish church and a well known music venue. Among those buried here are Vice-Admiral John Hunter, second Governor of New South Wales, and William Nash, an Irish recipient of the Victoria Cross.
